units.title: Vegetables
units.blurb: Blanching, glazing, roasting, purées and potatoes.

units.title: Grains, Pasta and Legumes
units.blurb: Rice and risotto, fresh pasta from scratch, beans and lentils.

topics.title: Blanching and Shocking
topics.short: Cook green vegetables briefly in plenty of salted boiling water, then plunge them into ice water to stop the cooking and keep the color bright.
topics.trouble: Cooks blanch too much at once, so the water stops boiling and the vegetables stew olive-green.

topics.title: Glazing, Roasting and Purées
topics.short: Glaze in a little water, butter and sugar until shiny; roast at high heat for browned edges; purée cooked vegetables and pass them through a sieve for smoothness.
topics.trouble: Cooks crowd a roasting pan, so vegetables steam instead of browning.

topics.title: Potatoes: Starchy and Waxy
topics.short: Starchy potatoes (russets) are fluffy for baking, mashing and frying; waxy ones hold their shape in salads and gratins. Classic fries are cooked twice: low, then high.
topics.trouble: Cooks mash potatoes in a blender or food processor, which makes them gluey.

topics.title: Rice, Grains and Risotto
topics.short: Absorption, pilaf and pasta methods; risotto adds hot stock a little at a time to short-grain rice while stirring, so the starch makes it creamy.
topics.trouble: Cooks rinse risotto rice or add cold stock, which slows it and spoils the creamy texture.

topics.title: Fresh Pasta from Scratch
topics.short: About 100 grams of flour for each large egg; knead until smooth, rest, roll thin, cut, and cook briefly in plenty of salted boiling water.
topics.trouble: Beginners roll pasta before it rests, and it springs back and tears.

topics.title: Beans and Lentils
topics.short: Sort and rinse; soak beans to shorten cooking; boil red kidney beans hard in fresh water to destroy a natural toxin; lentils need no soaking.
topics.trouble: Cooks simmer raw kidney beans in a slow cooker that never gets them to a full boil.
